added: Wall cabinets come in a variety of shapes and sizes and are used to store and/or display objects. Wall cabinets are generally very heavy and, additionally, they often support a lot of weight. For this reason, it is imperative to hang wall cabinets correctly, using builder-standard methods. You do not need to be a contractor, builder or handyman to install wall cabinets, but you do need to be able to follow instructions. If you are committed to installing your own wall-mounted cabinets, gather your materials, be prepared to do a certain amount of lifting and follow these steps for hanging wall cabinets.
#Plan your space. A standard, to-scale floor plan drawing will suffice for plotting out exactly where you want to install wall cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 1.jpg|center]]
#Determine if your floor is level.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 2.jpg|center]]
#Measure and make a mark 54 inches (137 cm) from the floor. If your floor is not level, measure from the highest point of the floor.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 3.jpg|center]]
#Draw a horizontal line at your mark. Use a level to ensure a straight and level line for hanging wall cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 4.jpg|center]]
#Find the wall studs using a stud finder. Mark the stud locations along the horizontal hanging line.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Secure ledger board along the hanging line. The ledger board will support your cabinets during installation. Screw the ledger board into the wall at the stud locations.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 6.jpg|center]]
#Remove all doors, handles and knobs from the cabinets.  This will ensure the lightest possible load while you hang wall cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Clamp together as many cabinets as you can safely lift. Use clamps to adjoin side-by-side vertical cabinet walls. Once they are clamped together, make sure the cabinet faces are flush.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Connect the cabinets. Pre-drill then screw the adjoining cabinets together in 4 places � 2 on the top and 2 on the bottom, on the far right and far left sides.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 9.jpg|center]]
#Lift the cabinets and rest them on the ledger board in their designated place. Check that they are level and plumb before moving on to the next step.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 10.jpg|center]]
#Pre-drill then screw the cabinets into the wall studs. Be sure to screw through the thick framing along the top of the cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 11.jpg|center]]
#Check for plumb and level after hanging wall cabinets and before moving on to hanging the next set of cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 12.jpg|center]]
#Repeat this process for each cabinet until all wall cabinets are hung.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 13.jpg|center]]
#Remove the ledger board.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 14.jpg|center]]
#Replace all the cabinet doors and hardware after you completely install wall cabinets.[[Image:Hang Wall Cabinets Step 15.jpg|center]]

revisions.summary: (Creating new article)

added: Wall cabinets come in a variety of shapes and sizes and are used to store and/or display objects. Wall cabinets are generally very heavy and, additionally, they often support a lot of weight. For this reason, it is imperative to hang wall cabinets correctly, using builder-standard methods. You do not need to be a contractor, builder or handyman to install wall cabinets, but you do need to be able to follow instructions. If you are committed to installing your own wall-mounted cabinets, gather your materials, be prepared to do a certain amount of lifting and follow these steps for hanging wall cabinets.
== Steps ==
# Plan your space. A standard, to-scale floor plan drawing will suffice for plotting out exactly where you want to install wall cabinets.
# Determine if your floor is level.
# Measure and make a mark 54 inches (137 cm) from the floor. If your floor is not level, measure from the highest point of the floor.
# Draw a horizontal line at your mark. Use a level to ensure a straight and level line for hanging wall cabinets.
# Find the wall studs using a stud finder. Mark the stud locations along the horizontal hanging line.
# Secure ledger board along the hanging line. The ledger board will support your cabinets during installation. Screw the ledger board into the wall at the stud locations.
# Remove all doors, handles and knobs from the cabinets.  This will ensure the lightest possible load while you hang wall cabinets.
# Clamp together as many cabinets as you can safely lift. Use clamps to adjoin side-by-side vertical cabinet walls. Once they are clamped together, make sure the cabinet faces are flush.
# Connect the cabinets. Pre-drill then screw the adjoining cabinets together in 4 places � 2 on the top and 2 on the bottom, on the far right and far left sides.
# Lift the cabinets and rest them on the ledger board in their designated place. Check that they are level and plumb before moving on to the next step.
# Pre-drill then screw the cabinets into the wall studs. Be sure to screw through the thick framing along the top of the cabinets.
# Check for plumb and level after hanging wall cabinets and before moving on to hanging the next set of cabinets.
# Repeat this process for each cabinet until all wall cabinets are hung.
# Remove the ledger board.
# Replace all the cabinet doors and hardware after you completely install wall cabinets.
== Tips ==
* Measure, level and plumb twice before you nail anything into place.
* Pay attention to the location of your electrical wiring and plumbing when deciding where to nail.
* If you plan on installing flooring after hanging wall cabinets, be sure to include the thickness of the flooring in the measurement for your horizontal hanging line.
* Use shims, if needed, to make cabinets plumb and level before securing them to the wall.
== Things You'll Need ==
* Tape measure
* Pencil
* Stud finder
* Drill
* Screws
* Level
* Shims
* Ledger board
* Clamps
